card.name: Words in all-caps boxed warnings
card.fires_on: Words and word endings inside all-capital warning text, such as boxed warnings on liver failure or blood reactions. It often sits on a linking word or a word ending just before the verb or next clause.

modes.label: Linking words
modes.description: Small linking words like AND or CAN that join clauses in capitalized warning text.
modes.example: THESE REACTIONS OCCUR RARELY<< AND>> GENERALLY IN PATIENTS RECEIVING

modes.label: Word endings
modes.description: Final pieces of long capitalized words such as plural endings or -ING, just before the sentence continues.

modes.label: Noun completing a phrase
modes.description: The last word of a capitalized noun phrase, such as FUNCTION or RATE, before the verb.
modes.example: CURRENT ESTIMATES OF THE OVERALL CASE FATALITY<< RATE>> ARE IN THE RANGE OF 20

card.writes: It promotes capitalized-style code-like starters such as For, And, In and All, which suggests a weak push toward starting a new capitalized item, while it suppresses bracket-led code tokens.
card.plain: It lights up in ALL-CAPS warning paragraphs, on small joining words and word endings in the middle of a sentence.
